_comments: LAYERED BASE VIEW on Contracts (plan item 12). CodeGen writes its full generated view under
GeneratedBaseViewName (vwContractsGenerated) and the APP owns BaseView (vwContracts) as a thin
wrapper adding the derived columns: State (ERD §4.5), IsAwaitingDocument, IsChangeOrder,
DaysToEnd, RenewalNoticeDeadline, IsInCancellationWindow.
THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE OF RECORD for these two flags. The migration train also sets them, and
that is not redundancy — metadata is only consolidated into a migration at end-of-version, so in
the window before that a fresh environment runs migrate → codegen → sync push, and that FIRST
codegen would see BaseViewGenerated = 1, resolve its target to the PUBLIC name, and DROP/CREATE
vwContracts as a plain generated view — silently destroying the hand-written wrapper. Orders
documents the trap in V202608131541__…_layered_inner_view.sql and it cost them real time.
Keyed by entity NAME. Entity IDs are minted by CodeGen on first registration, so a hardcoded UUID
stops matching the first time this database is rebuilt from zero.
FORM CHROME on Contracts (D-17). Layout 'left-nav': the rail down the left side decides what the
body shows, one section at a time — it ROUTES rather than scrolling an accordion. The contract
form has enough distinct concerns (identity, dates, renewal terms, modifications, documents,
lineage, history) that an accordion makes the reader hunt.
RelatedRolePolicy 'smart' + PrimaryRelatedBudget 6: the same settings orders carries on every
entity. 'smart' lets the ranker place related entities we have not explicitly ruled on in
.form-chrome.json, and the budget caps how many earn a primary slot before the rest go to More.
An earlier draft said Layout 'auto' was fine at this section count. Superseded by D-17 — matching
orders matters more than the marginal call, because a user moving between the two apps should not
have to learn two form idioms.
FORM CHROME on Contract Templates. Same left-nav treatment: a template version is identity plus a
provision list plus the source document, and the provisions editor (item 7) wants the full body
width rather than an accordion panel's.
Marcelo ruled a custom form here so provisions are visible as the template's real content rather
than a related grid below the fields — that is a PANEL claiming the related entity (plan §6.4),
so the chrome stays stock and only the section content changes.
